Article Title: Disha Salian death case: CBI registers FIR, takes over probe from Mumbai Police
Article Text:
The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years

NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput , days after the Bombay high court ordered a central agency probe into the case.The FIR follows the high court's September 2 order directing the CBI to register a case and conduct a fresh investigation into Salian's death. The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years, observing that it "raises more questions than answers".The bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale had said a case investigation could not continue for an inordinately long period and directed the CBI to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to investigate the matter.The court also directed the Mumbai Police to hand over all case papers to the CBI and record the statement of Salian's father, Satish Salian. It made clear that registration of the FIR did not mean that anyone would automatically be treated as an accused."Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless, in the opinion of the investigating officer, there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation," the court said.Salian, 28, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai's Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) and, following an inquiry, concluded that her death was a suicide.The high court pointed to what it described as "glaring discrepancies" in the police investigation, including the timing of the spot panchnama and questions concerning injuries sustained by Salian.Salian's father had approached the high court alleging that his daughter was raped and murdered and seeking a CBI investigation. He had also sought an FIR against Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, though the high court refrained from making findings against any individual.Salian had briefly worked as Rajput's manager. Rajput was found dead at his Mumbai residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian's death. A separate CBI probe into Rajput's death was ordered, with the agency later filing a closure report stating that he died by suicide.
Article Summary: CBI has registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput. The Bombay high court had ordered a central agency probe into the case. The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR.

Article Title: 'As India leads, world listens': Rajnath Singh hails 18th Brics joint declaration
Article Text:
"As India leads, the world listens," Rajnath Singh posted on X.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh Monday hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly, saying the unison adaptation was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi Calling "inclusive and human-centric approach" an hallmark of the summit, the defence minister laid emphasis on how the bloc put Global South "at the centre, not at the margins, championing a more inclusive, representative and balanced world order"."Rooted in our civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiv Kutumbkam, India has once again shown that leadership is not about having the loudest voice, but the strongest consensus," the Union minister said, adding: "As India leads, the world listens."In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The talks were complicated by differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict. An earlier meeting of Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had also ended without a joint statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi after a rare meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit.The meeting took place as the conflict continued and helped ease the differences threatening consensus.The declaration used carefully balanced language to address the concerns of both countries. It expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities operating under full International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, describing such actions as violations of international law and relevant IAEA resolutions. The wording amounted to an implicit criticism of US and Israeli strikes on Iran and was important in securing Tehran’s approval.The leaders also recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to maintain the smooth movement of global trade, supply chains and energy in line with international law.Official sources said India conducted prolonged negotiations at several levels to bridge the differences between Iran and the UAE. Other member-states also supported the effort, keen to ensure that the summit ended with a joint declaration rather than another failure to reach consensus.The agreement recalled the last-minute G20 declaration adopted in New Delhi in 2023 during the Russia-Ukraine war. That statement used carefully worded language urging countries not to use force to seize territory without directly naming Russia.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly. Singh said the unison adaptation was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration.

Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti- West. PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"

Article Title: Kremlin says PM Modi, Xi offered Putin their 'good offices' to help end Ukraine war

Russia on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered their services to help end the Ukraine war on the sidelines of the Brics summit According to news agency Reuters, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed their readiness.“During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in the Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution,” Peskov said.This comes amid US President Donald Trump's ongoing efforts to broker a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.PM Modi and Putin also held a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the summit and discussed closer trade ties, including implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, as well as cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence and culture.They had earlier met on the sidelines of the Shanghai cooperation organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek on August 31.“Delighted to meet President Putin in Delhi, less than two weeks after our meeting in Bishkek. Article Title: 'I resign as CM': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke mocks MP govt after Balaghat heckling

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday mocked the Mohan Yadav-led Madhya Pradesh government and announced his resignation as the state's chief minister.The sarcastic announcement came after Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat district, where more than 30 tribal children have reportedly died from infectious diseases.In a post on X, Dipke wrote: "I hereby resign as the chief minister of MP with immediate effect. I thank Hon’ble PM @narendramodi ji for giving me the opportunity to serve the people of MP, an opportunity in which I have clearly failed."Dipke also shared a purported resignation letter addressed to the Madhya Pradesh governor, in which he took responsibility for the deaths of the tribal children and criticised the state government's response to the tragedy."My conscience does not allow me to continue occupying this chair after the deaths of more than 30 Tribal children in Balaghat. As Chief Minister, I accept responsibility for failing to provide them with the timely medical care and support they needed," the letter said.Dipke further questioned the compensation announced for the victims and alleged that the government had initially offered a lower amount before increasing it following protests by the tribal community."Our response reflects how little value we have placed on the lives of Tribal children," the letter said, while also questioning why health officials had not been held accountable.The CJP founder's post came after his visit to Adori, Korka and Bondari villages in Balaghat, where he met families of tribal children who allegedly died from infectious diseases and gathered information about healthcare facilities.During the visit, a viral video showed a woman, described as a social media influencer, approaching Dipke with a microphone as he was leaving in a car. She questioned whether he had come to "do politics on corpses" and why he had visited the area so late.Dipke was heard apologising for the delayed visit. The woman was also heard saying, "A good road has been constructed here. Can't you see it?"As the confrontation escalated, CJP workers accompanying Dipke moved him into another car and took him away. The woman was then heard saying, "he ran away, he ran away."
Article Summary: The sarcastic announcement came after Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat district. Dipke also shared a purported resignation letter addressed to the Madhya Pradesh governor, in which he took responsibility for the deaths of the tribal children.

New Delhi: Congress Sunday accused PM Modi of "calibrated capitulation" before China, claiming the trade deficit with the neighbour has ballooned to unprecedented levels.A day after the meeting between President Xi Jinping and Modi, AICC spokesman Jairam Ramesh asked four questions to the PM, ranging from his statement giving a "clean chit" to China after the Galwan clashes to "allowing" a dilution in India's stance about China-Pakistan nexus during Operation Sindoor.Ramesh asked Modi, "Did not your infamous clean chit to China - Na koi humari seema mein ghus aaya hai, na hi koi ghusa hua hai - on June 19, 2020 weaken India?" Article Title: A year on, Rs 15 lakh for kin of 4 killed in Leh firing
Article Text:
Violence broke out in Leh on September 24 last year

SRINAGAR: Ladakh lieutenant governor VK Saxena announced Sunday Rs 15 lakh compensation for the next of kin of each of the four protesters killed in police firing during violent protests in Leh on Sept 24 last year.The firing left around 90 protesters wounded as demonstrations demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards under Schedule Six for the Union territory turned violent. “An ex gratia of Rs 3 lakh for those with major injuries and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries has also been approved,” Saxena said.The LG thanked Union home minister Amit Shah for his “sensitive, humanitarian and guiding approach”, saying he had “always stood in solidarity with the victims and their families”.Leh Apex Body co-chairperson Chering Dorjay Lakrook had repeatedly sought compensation for victims during meetings with the home ministry. After a Sept 9 meeting this year, Ladakh groups said Centre had assured them it would withdraw cases against those arrested during last year’s protests and provide compensation to victims and wounded protesters.Authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions in Leh after the violence, suspended mobile internet and arrested more than 80 people. FIRs were registered against 87, including activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was charged under NSA and kept in Jodhpur jail until March this year.
Article Summary: Ladakh lieutenant governor VK Saxena announced Sunday Rs 15 lakh compensation for the next of kin of each of the four protesters killed in police firing. The firing left around 90 protesters wounded as demonstrations demanding statehood and constitutional safeguards for the Union territory turned violent.

Article Title: 'Not our culture to impose Emergency, we believe in dialogue': Amit Shah on Gen-Z led movements
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government believes in dialogue and discussion while addressing questions on the social and political impact of various Gen Z-led movements.Shah said at a press conference that people in a democracy have the right to express their views, asserting that a BJP-led government cannot impose an Emergency."We are in a democracy. People hold different views on various issues, and it is essential that those views are expressed. The Bharatiya Janata Party is in power, but we cannot govern by imposing an Emergency. That is the Congress culture, not ours. We believe in dialogue and discussion," Shah said.Asked whether the National Register of Citizens (NRC) would be implemented in Manipur using the 1951 baseline before the elections, and whether there was a deadline for its nationwide implementation, Shah said the government was discussing the issues with its colleagues and political parties in Manipur."We are discussing both these matters with our colleagues as well as with the political parties in Manipur. As soon as any decision is taken, we will inform you," he said.On tensions over language and regional identity linked to migration, Shah said the government’s policy was to give priority to the mother tongue, adding that the Constitution had laid down specific directives for states on the issue.\"It is our government's policy to prioritise the mother tongue, and the Constitution has also issued specific directives to the states in this regard. I do not believe this will become a major issue. While isolated incidents may occur if certain individuals attempt to stoke tensions, the states have experienced leadership and will certainly find a way to resolve such issues," Shah added.He also added that PM Modi was the first prime minister in six decades, since the early years after Independence, to be elected to office three times, calling it a reflection of his 25-year political record.Shah said the country had pursued a strong foreign and defence policy based on the principle of “India First”, while the economy had risen from being counted among the ‘Fragile Five’ to the world’s top five. He also cited 7.8 per cent GDP growth in the first quarter as evidence of India’s strong economic performance.Shah was addressing a press conference to announce the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan”, scheduled from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday and his 25 years in public life in Gujarat and at the Centre.Shah said the BJP, its allies and people across the country would jointly organise the month-long campaign from September 17, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.He said the BJP had earlier observed Modi’s birthday as ‘Seva Saptah’ from September 17 to October 2, while some places extended the celebrations for a week. However, this year’s celebrations would be special as Modi will complete 25 years in public office as chief minister and prime minister on October 7.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the government believes in dialogue and discussion. Shah was addressing a press conference to announce the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, scheduled from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.

Article Title: 'Unacceptable': India condemns attack on commercial vessel off Oman, 13 Indians rescued
Article Text:
India condemns attack, 13 of 14 Indian crew rescued from vessel off Oman (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: India on Sunday condemned an attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman, saying 13 of the 14 Indian crew members onboard had been rescued while search and rescue operations continued for the missing Indian national.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said the Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities. The statement came as an Iranian cargo vessel was also reported to have been struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting one death and four injuries.“We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman earlier today. Of the 14 Indian crew onboard, 13 Indians have been rescued so far. Search and Rescue operations for the missing Indian national are continuing,” the MEA said.The ministry said it had reiterated India's call for immediate de-escalation and the use of dialogue and diplomacy to restore peace in the region.The MEA said the targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians and civilian infrastructure in the region was unacceptable.“We reiterate our call for immediate de-escalation of tensions and pursuance of dialogue and diplomacy to bring peace to the region. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable,” it said.India also called for the restoration of safe navigation and commercial traffic through international waterways in the region.“We also urge that free and safe navigation and flow of commerce through the international waterways in the region be restored at the earliest,” the MEA said.The Indian statement came amid renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, where an Iranian cargo vessel was reportedly struck early Sunday near Qeshm Island.Iranian state media said the attack killed one person and wounded four others. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitor separately said a vessel had been hit by a projectile while transiting the strait, triggering a fire and an evacuation operation, although it was not immediately clear whether it was the same incident.Iran's state-run IRNA quoted the governor of Qeshm as blaming a “terrorist enemy” for the attack.Hours before the reported strike, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said: “Our people can’t be bullied into submission. Iran won’t surrender,” according to a social media post.The attacks came a day before a planned meeting of foreign ministers from regional countries in Oman to discuss efforts by Iran and Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Iran has said that an agreement with Oman on managing the waterway would not automatically mean that the strait would be reopened to shipping. Pezeshkian told India Today TV on Saturday: “The waterway would be opened up on the condition that the U.S. will terminate its blockade.”
Article Summary: India condemns attack, 13 of 14 Indian crew rescued from vessel off Oman. Search and rescue operations continue for missing Indian national. Iranian cargo vessel was also reported to have been struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting one death.

Article Title: Nepal floods: 80 still missing after two weeks of disaster, says Isha Foundation
Article Text:
77 pilgrims, 3 volunteers of Isha Foundation remain unaccounted for

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two weeks after flash floods struck the Nepal-Tibet border, 77 participants of a Kailash Manasarovar pilgrimage and three volunteers remain unaccounted for, the Isha Foundation said in a statement, adding that the figure has not changed since its previous update.The foundation said identification work at the disaster site was still under way and authorities had indicated that the process could take considerable time.According to the statement, Isha Foundation has remained in contact with Chinese, Indian and Nepali authorities, as well as embassies representing 19 countries in India, Nepal and China, to seek information about those affected and relay verified updates to families.The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rose to 1,386 on Saturday as rescuers recovered more bodies from eight affected districts, authorities said.The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages across northern and central Nepal.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said 5,130 people remain missing, while 13,728 have been rescued so far.Only 104 bodies have been identified and handed over to families. Meanwhile, 339 people are receiving treatment in 19 hospitals and 3,761 displaced people are staying in 37 holding centres.The foundation said identification details, photographs and other relevant material had been shared with authorities and search-and-rescue teams where required. It also said its volunteers had been in touch with the US state department and Global Affairs Canada, whose assistance in seeking information from Chinese authorities had been useful."Any new information that can appropriately be shared will be communicated to the affected families first and made public where it is legal, ethical, and appropriate to do so", Isha foundation said.Access to the affected site at Gyirong Port on the Chinese side of the Nepal-Tibet border remains restricted by Chinese authorities for rescue and forensic work, while access on the Nepal side is also restricted by Nepali authorities, the foundation said.“No private individuals or organisations have been allowed near the site,” it said, adding that Isha volunteers who had been stationed in Gyirong Town were asked by Chinese authorities to leave along with other non-official personnel.In Nepal, around 25 Nepali volunteers are supporting efforts on the ground, according to the statement. The team has been coordinating with hospitals, mortuaries, police and government offices and has shared information on missing individuals with the Nepal Police and Nepal Tourist Police.The foundation said contact had also been established with the Nepali Army and that details of those missing had been passed to personnel involved in search-and-rescue efforts.Following the floods, volunteers visited hospitals and mortuaries to gather information and understand identification procedures, the statement said. The team also visited a DNA centre to understand the requirements for identification, with the process being coordinated through the respective countries' consular services.Isha said information received from embassies and authorities was being passed to the affected families, particularly emergency contacts, along with details of the next steps.The foundation said international media were granted access on the 12th day after the disaster, but that subsequent reports had not yielded new facts.It added that a volunteer team was responding to calls and emails through a dedicated hotline operating across eight countries. Families are also being assisted with practical arrangements, including the shipment of belongings left behind in Kathmandu.The foundation said it would continue coordinating with authorities and emergency services and share verified information with families as it becomes available.
Article Summary: The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rose to 1,386 on Saturday as rescuers recovered more bodies. The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages across northern and central Nepal.

Article Title: Rajasthan SET 2026: Students boycott exam in Jaipur over delayed papers, alleged irregularities
Article Text:
(Representative image): The candidates also alleged that they were asked to either enter the examination hall and remain quiet or leave when they questioned officials about the delay.

Candidates claim exam was cancelled

Exam irregularities have repeatedly triggered protests

Students walked out of a Rajasthan State Eligibility Test (SET-2026) centre in Jaipur on Sunday after alleging that question papers were distributed nearly 30 minutes after the scheduled start, triggering protests and a boycott over what they described as serious exam irregularities.The disruption took place at Pink City Senior Secondary School on Bainar Road, where candidates said the exam was due to begin at 11am. They alleged that the question papers did not reach the centre until around 11.30am. Several candidates then left the centre and protested outside.The candidates also alleged that they were asked to either enter the examination hall and remain quiet or leave when they questioned officials about the delay.Anita Lamba, one of the candidates, questioned whether the same leniency would be extended to students who reached an examination centre even a minute after the gate-closing time."When we questioned the institution, they threatened us, saying that if we wanted to give the exam, we should go inside and sit quietly, or we could leave...This has been happening with children in the past, continues to happen, and will happen in the future," she told reporters.The situation escalated after candidates approached the police and raised their concerns with authorities present at the centre.Lamba said that after discussions with the police, the principal showed the candidates a notice stating that "the exam is being cancelled"."We have accepted the fact that the exam is cancelled," she said.However, there was no official notification confirming cancellation of the examination at the time of reporting.Another candidate, Sania Kaval, alleged that students were repeatedly asked to wait for five or 10 minutes as they waited for the question papers to arrive. When the papers eventually came, candidates were reportedly told that they would be given additional time to compensate for the delay."The invigilator at my centre was an 11th-grade student; she was signing papers as clumsily as a toddler might scribble. We asked why the paper hadn't arrived by 11:00 AM, and they told us it was on the way, asking us to wait for five minutes, then another ten minutes. The paper still didn't arrive, and when it came ten minutes late, they said we would get extra time...we want the cancelled exam to be held again, and second, we want this centre to be cancelled," she told ANI.Candidates said they ultimately agreed to appear for the examination after raising their concerns with the authorities. However, the delay and the manner in which the situation was handled led to a boycott by students at the centre.The Jaipur episode comes against a wider backdrop of repeated complaints over the conduct of competitive and government recruitment examinations in India. Delayed papers, question-paper leaks, impersonation, technical failures and allegations of administrative lapses have repeatedly led to cancellations, re-examinations and protests by aspirants.The Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers (REET) has previously been hit by question-paper leak allegations and other irregularities, while the state has also seen recruitment examinations disrupted by paper leaks and cheating allegations. The Rajasthan Police constable recruitment examination, for instance, had a paper leak controversy in 2022, leading authorities to cancel the affected paper and order a re-examination.For the SET candidates in Jaipur, the immediate demand is for clarity on whether Sunday's examination will stand or be cancelled. They have also demanded that the Bainar Road centre be removed from future examinations and that the test be conducted again if it is formally cancelled.
Article Summary: Candidates claim exam was cancelled at Pink City Senior Secondary School in Jaipur. They alleged that question papers did not reach the centre until around 11.30am. They also alleged that they were asked to either enter the examination hall and remain quiet or leave when they questioned officials.

NEW DELHI: Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday accused the PM Modi-led Centre of giving the state "stepmotherly" treatment in flood relief, while seeking a "national disaster" tag for the flood situation.Addressing a press conference in Patna, the RJD working president criticised chief minister Samrat Choudhary and Union ministers from Bihar for "failing to secure a relief package for Bihar"."Whenever there are floods in Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi gives quick assurances of relief, talks to state leadership and directs deployment of relief forces, including the Indian Air Force. NEW DELHI: Mayawati on Sunday escalated her criticism of her nephew Akash Anand, saying he continues to act under the influence of his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, days after Anand was 'fully relieved' from the party. The Bahujan Samaj Party chief also accused expelled leaders of attempting to create confusion among BSP workers by spreading rumours about her health.The remarks came after Mayawati removed Akash as the party’s national coordinator on September 3 and subsequently announced that he had been relieved from the BSP. On Saturday, she ruled out political roles for Akash and his brother Ishan Anand, describing the move as her “final decision”.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Mayawati said she had learnt of an alleged phone call made by Akash to Alok Kumar, a party in-charge at her residence, in which he enquired about her health.“It seems that people who have been expelled from the party have been spreading confusion among party members for the past 1-2 days that Behen Ji (Mayawati) is quite ill,” she said.Mayawati said Akash asked Kumar, “whether Behen Ji is ill? Article Title: MPSC paper leak: CJP to join protesters demanding resignation of key officials, sets Sept 24 deadline

Article Title: UK breakup on menu? Leaders of Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales to meet
Article Text:
When Trump said a "unified Ireland is going to happen eventually," he might have known something UK PM Andy Burnham didn't.

A day after President Trump expressed his support for Northern Ireland breaking from the UK to unify with the Republic of Ireland, the leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are gathering at a summit in Cardiff to sign a deal designed to kick-start the break-up of the United Kingdom.The three first ministers, all representing pro-independence parties thanks to Labour's disastrous performance at devolved elections in May, will call on British govt to "prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change" in Wales, Scotland and the north of Ireland.Leader of the Scottish National Party John Swinney, Leader of Plaid Cymru Rhun ap Iorwerth, Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald and Sinn Fein Vice-President Michelle O'Neill issued a statement Sunday to say they are meeting in Cardiff to "strengthen the cooperation of Wales, Scotland and Ireland" and build towards constitutional change.When Trump said a "unified Ireland is going to happen eventually," he might have known something UK PM Andy Burnham didn't. At Prime Minister's Questions last week Burnham made the strange comment that both in Scotland and Northern Ireland a border poll would be considered if there was a clear consensus that public opinion had changed - even though this is only the case for Northern Ireland. Scotland has no equivalent statutory trigger.He was then forced to write a letter to Swinney saying that independence and a referendum in Scotland "are off limits". "Burnham doesn't seem to know the basics of the UK Government's position on the Union," a source close to Swinney told the Sunday Telegraph.Swinney said on Sunday: "We are at a pivotal moment of constitutional change, and our parties share the common belief that our interests will never be served by Westminster, and that the people of our respective nations must have a meaningful say over their future."
Article Summary: Leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are gathering at a summit in Cardiff to sign a deal designed to kick-start the break-up of the United Kingdom. The three first ministers, all representing pro-independence parties thanks to Labour's disastrous performance at devolved elections, will call on British govt to "prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change"

Article Title: ABVP protests Umar Khalid documentary screening at NLSIU
