Article Title: ‘Plane started to plummet’: Passengers scream as Turkish Airlines flight hits turbulence
Article Text: Passengers screamed as severe turbulence jolted a Turkish Airlines flight from Istanbul to Tunisia during its descent on Thursday, with one traveller saying the aircraft “started to plummet” after three attempts to land in stormy conditions.The flight was approaching Tunis-Carthage International Airport when bad weather disrupted the landing. The aircraft was eventually diverted to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport, around 60 miles south of Tunis.Passenger Marina Maiskaya shared a video of the incident on Instagram, showing passengers gripping their seats as the aircraft shook and screams could be heard throughout the cabin.“The flight itself was smooth, but things turned absolutely terrifying as soon as we began our descent,” she wrote.“I have never in my life feared for my life like that, and my mom was with me, too.”Maiskaya said the pilot made three attempts to land at Tunis-Carthage International Airport while flying through the storm.“The pilot tried to land the plane at the same airport three times, flying right through a storm! We were shaken violently each time, and on the third attempt, we actually started to plummet,” she wrote.Passengers could be heard screaming as the aircraft appeared to suddenly lose altitude. “Here we started to fall down for a few seconds like free falling,” she said in the video.However, TOI could not independently verify the video. The aircraft was eventually diverted to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport, where it landed safely.
Article Summary: Turkish Airlines flight from Istanbul to Tunisia diverted to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport. Passenger Marina Maiskaya shared a video of the incident on Instagram. She said the pilot made three attempts to land at Tunis-Carthage International Airport while flying through a storm.

Article Title: 'A ceremony of light': First-ever Ganga Aarti held on River Thames in London - video
Article Text:
Ganga Aarti on the Thames. (Photo credit: PTI)

Thousands of people gathered on the banks of the River Thames on Sunday for the first-ever Ganga Aarti in London, a traditional Hindu ceremony of light and thanksgiving.Titled “Ganga Aarti on the Thames: A Ceremony of Light”, the event was organised by Chinmaya Mission UK in collaboration with the annual Totally Thames festival. It was part of global celebrations marking the 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission.The ceremony recreated the spirit of the world-famous Ganga Aarti held along the River Ganges in India. Organisers described it as a symbol of the life-giving flow of nature, knowledge and consciousness.“For generations, communities have gathered on the banks of Ganga to offer light in gratitude for the river, for nature and for all that sustains life,” said Brahmacharini Shripriya Chaitanya, resident teacher of Chinmaya Mission UK, according to PTI.“Ganga Aarti on the Thames carries that same spirit, bringing people together in a shared moment of gratitude, hope and unity,” she added.The traditional ceremony involved large, multi-tiered oil lamps, prayers, music and chanting. It was held against the backdrop of the historic Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich and brought together spiritual leaders, representatives of Hindu organisations and members of South Asian communities from across the UK.Chaitanya said the River Ganges also symbolised the flow of knowledge for Chinmaya Mission. “Our founder, Swami Chinmayananda, dedicated his life to bringing the timeless wisdom of Vedanta -- one of the great philosophical traditions of Hinduism, from the Himalayas into people's everyday lives. As we mark 75 years of Chinmaya Mission, this event is also a celebration of that legacy: of knowledge, service and gratitude flowing beyond boundaries,” she said, PTI reported.The ceremony took place entirely on land, with no material from the event placed, poured or released into the River Thames.Chinmaya Mission UK said the event was intended as a celebration for the British Hindu and wider South Asian communities, while also inviting people of all backgrounds to reflect on gratitude and respect for nature.“At its heart, Ganga Aarti reminds us not to take the natural world for granted. Gratitude towards nature should be expressed not only through prayer, but through the care and responsibility with which we treat the environment around us,” the organisation said.Chinmaya Mission, founded in 1951, is a global movement focused on spiritual education, inner transformation and the teachings of Vedanta. It has more than 350 centres worldwide and runs cultural, educational and service initiatives. The first Ganga Aarti event, which was sold out, is expected to pave the way for it to become a more regular annual feature of the festival.
Article Summary: Ganga Aarti is a traditional Hindu ceremony of light and thanksgiving. It was held on the banks of the River Thames in London as part of global celebrations. The event was organised by Chinmaya Mission UK in collaboration with Totally Thames festival.

Article Title: Trump rejects calls to slow AI, says US leads China in technology
Article Text: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said the United States is leading China in artificial intelligence and must maintain its edge, declaring that “whoever wins AI wins” as he pushed back against calls for the industry to slow down or face tighter regulation.“We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” Trump told reporters when asked if the AI industry should slow down or be more regulated.Trump acknowledged that authorities could introduce safeguards for AI but said concerns being raised about the technology were often exaggerated.“We could put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen,” Trump said.His comments come as the United States and China compete for dominance in AI, with Washington seeking to preserve its technological advantage in a rapidly evolving industry.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump says the U.S. is leading China in artificial intelligence. He pushed back against calls for the industry to slow down or face tighter regulation. His comments come as the United States and China compete for dominance in AI.

Article Title: Jharkhand businessman murder: How did traffic cop track victim’s phone? CP orders probe
Article Text:
Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand

Traffic sergeant arrested in murder case

TOI





KOLKATA: Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand has ordered a high-level internal probe following the arrest of traffic police sergeant Ayan Gupta, a 2010-batch officer posted at the Beliaghata Traffic Guard, by Jharkhand Police in connection with the Aug 24 murder of a Jharkhand-based businessman.Gupta’s arrest revealed that he had allegedly supplied the accused with cell-tower locations and call records at the behest of Beliaghata Traffic Guard civic volunteer Twinkle Das, who allegedly maintained contact with the killers. A traffic sergeant in Kolkata Police is not authorised to access or provide such data.After the matter came to light, Nand ordered the internal probe. The local traffic guard has completed its preliminary inquiry and submitted its findings to Lalbazar. The police headquarters is now seeking to fix responsibility and ascertain whether anyone else was involved.Senior officers at Lalbazar said the top brass was closely monitoring the probe. Nand also confirmed tovia text message that the inquiry was underway, though he did not provide details.Investigators have learnt that Gupta allegedly supplied businessman Nikhil’s mobile tower location to Raghav, who is suspected to be the mastermind behind the murder.Twinkle, said to be a close associate of Raghav, has also been arrested.According to police sources, Gupta, a Parnasree resident, acted on requests from Twinkle, who lives in the Chaulpatti Road area. Gupta allegedly accessed Nikhil’s mobile tower location multiple times and passed the information to Raghav. Police suspect the location data was used to track Nikhil and plan his killing.Only authorised investigating officers in the Detective Department — including those attached to the Cyber Crime Branch or assigned to specific cases — and specialised technical units such as the Kolkata Police’s Special Task Force can officially seek and access mobile tower location data from telecom service providers, and only after obtaining the requisite legal permissions.“Ordinary citizens — and not even traffic police personnel — can directly request mobile tower logs or location-tracking data because of privacy and legal restrictions,” said a senior officer.Last Thursday, a Jharkhand Police team summoned Gupta and Twinkle to Lalbazar, where they were questioned at length by officers of the Detective Department. Sources said the entire interrogation was videographed. They were subsequently informed of their arrest.On Aug 24, businessman Nikhil was shot dead in front of a hotel along NH 33 in the Chandil police station area. Police said the attackers fired around nine rounds, hitting him in the shoulder, back and neck. He was taken in critical condition to a hospital in Jamshedpur, where doctors declared him dead.Although the case initially appeared to stem from business rivalry, the probe increasingly pointed to a contract killing.Police suspect the shooters were paid nearly Rs 15 lakh. Investigators are now focusing on the alleged illegal sharing of mobile location data.
Article Summary: Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand has ordered a high-level internal probe following the arrest of traffic police sergeant Ayan Gupta. Gupta allegedly supplied businessman Nikhil’s mobile tower location to Raghav, who is suspected to be the mastermind behind the murder.

Article Title: Left to contest in Tamil Nadu bypolls but continue to back TVK govt
Article Text:
CPM state secretary P Shanmugam making the announcement in Trichy





TRICHY/CHENNAI: CPI and CPM have decided to contest the Oct 6 byelections in Madurantakam and Dharapuram, emphasising their position of political non-alignment with TVK while backing its govt to “keep BJP away”.CPM state secretary P Shanmugam on Sunday announced his party would contest in Madurantakam and that CPI would field a candidate in Dharapuram. The candidates would be announced on Sept 15, said CPI state secretary M Veerapandian.The decision was taken at state committee meetings of the two parties in Trichy and Chennai. Their support for the TVK-led govt, however, would continue, the leaders said.Though CPI and CPM have been critical of TVK, the decision has come as a surprise for many because the Left would have to campaign against the govt they support, said political watchers.Defending the decision, Shanmugam said support for the govt does not mean CPM should not adopt a position to strengthen the organisation. He said contesting the byelections did not mean that CPM was threatening the stability of TVK govt.“Nor does it mean that we support DMK. Left parties are not part of any of the three alliances. This is not a general election or an election to change govt,” he said.Veerapandian echoed the same. The Left leaders said the bypolls would be used to strengthen their presence in the assembly and amplify the voice of workers and ordinary people.“There was a strong sentiment in our executive committee meeting for this position,” he said. Shanmugam took an indirect dig at TVK for accommodating the resigned AIADMK MLAs, which has resulted in the bypoll.“We have said it was wrong for two MLAs — who won on the AIADMK symbol in the assembly election — to resign and join TVK, and that horse-trading was involved,” he said.He said their campaign would focus on TVK govt’s performance and the issues on which the Left had differed with it.“We have expressed our differences of opinion on many occasions, including the budget. We have urged ministers on what laws should be passed and not passed. A few were accepted, but many were not. We have urged that the legislative assembly should serve as a democratic forum for discussing people’s issues. All this will find focus in the campaign,” he said.Veerapandian said drug abuse, law and order problems and lack of infrastructure would be raised in their campaignThe decision is seen as an extension of the Left’s stand of “supporting the govt to prevent a BJP intrusion”. The Left skipped an alliance meeting chaired by the CM, marking the second such successive boycott.
Article Summary: CPI and CPM have decided to contest the Oct 6 byelections in Madurantakam and Dharapuram. The decision was taken at state committee meetings of the two parties in Trichy and Chennai. Their support for the TVK-led govt, however, would continue.

Article Title: DNA test links bike mechanic to Telangana nurse’s rape-murder
Article Text:
Forensic examination of other exhibits collected from the scene also yielded findings supporting the DNA match, sources said.

Telangana nurse murder case

Mechanic lived near victim’s room

Forensics strengthens police case





HYDERABAD: DNA analysis by Telangana Forensic Science Laboratory (TGFSL) has linked accused Md Sanaullah, 34, to the alleged rape and murder of a 21-year-old nurse at Tukkuguda, providing forensic corroboration to police investigation.Sources in Pahadishareef police said investigators have received the forensic report, which found that the DNA profile generated from biological material collected from the victim’s private parts matched the accused’s DNA profile.Forensic examination of other exhibits collected from the scene also yielded findings supporting the DNA match, sources said. The DNA examination was carried out by TGFSL DNA division.Sanaullah, a bike mechanic and native of Begusarai district in Bihar, had come to Hyderabad in 2023. At the time of the offence, he was working and staying at a mechanic shop in Tukkuguda, close to the accommodation where the nurse lived.The nurse, who worked at a private hospital in Tukkuguda, was found dead in her room on Aug 29 after colleagues became concerned when she did not respond.Police initially registered a murder case under BNS Section 103 while awaiting forensic findings on suspected sexual assault.Police detained Sanaullah on Aug 30 and later arrested him in the case.According to investigators, the accused had allegedly been watching the nurse’s movements for nearly a month. Police said he entered her room through a window while she was asleep and attempted to sexually assault her. When she resisted, he allegedly strangled her before escaping through the same window.Following the medical examination, police added rape provisions and sections of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Investigators had earlier relied on technical evidence, crime scene material, hair strands and other forensic evidence while questioning the accused. The latest DNA report provides scientific corroboration, linking him to the sexual assault, police sources said.
Article Summary: DNA analysis by Telangana Forensic Science Laboratory (TGFSL) has linked accused Md Sanaullah, 34, to the alleged rape and murder of a 21-year-old nurse. The nurse, who worked at a private hospital in Tukkuguda, was found dead in her room on Aug 29.

Article Title: Ludhiana encounter: Police shoot 2 hitmen 1km away from where they were to strike
Article Text:
The event was organised on Dugri Road in memory of former Congress village sarpanch Rajwinder Singh Grewal alias Ravi Khwajke





LUDHIANA: Police killed two suspected hitmen in an encounter Sunday afternoon, intercepting them just one km from a memorial event they were allegedly sent to attack in Ludhiana.Police commissioner Swapan Sharma said the two, identified as Karanjot Singh alias Nona and Sandeep Singh , both from Amritsar, were sent by wanted gangsters Balwinder Singh alias Dony Bal and Shaganpreet Singh, key operatives of the Davinder Bambiha gang, to open fire at a blood donation camp.The event was organised on Dugri Road in memory of former Congress village sarpanch Rajwinder Singh Grewal alias Ravi Khwajke, who was shot dead by Bambiha and his associates during a wedding function near Gill Road on Feb 20, 2016.Joint teams from the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) and Ludhiana city police engaged the suspects who were on a motorcycle near the Atam Nagar police post after receiving an intelligence tip-off.Sharma said the suspects opened fire on police officers after being cornered, hitting a police vehicle twice during an exchange of more than 25 rounds before being shot dead in retaliatory fire.Police recovered three 9mm automatic handguns, including a Turkish-made Zigana and a Pakistani Glock, along with 50 live rounds and a motorcycle from the encounter site.Police said the weapons were smuggled across the border.Police suspect their additional accomplices on separate vehicles may have escaped.Both the shooters had criminal background. While Karanjot had been booked in Arms Act, robbery and NDPS Act cases, Sandeep faced one criminal case, according to police.AGTF deputy superintendent Rajan Parminder Singh said, “Police suspect the gunmen had a particular target to kill at the memorial. However, the kind of weapons and ammunition they were carrying, they could have caused multiple casualties.”Police investigations are ongoing.In Jan 2022, a local court convicted a Moga resident and sentenced him to rigorous life imprisonment in the 2016 Khwajke murder case. Three other accused, Bambiha, Kamaljit Singh Bunty and Jaspreet Singh Jumpy, had died in separate police encounters.
Article Summary: The event was organised on Dugri Road in memory of former Congress village sarpanch Rajwinder Singh Grewal alias Ravi Khwajke. Police recovered three 9mm automatic handguns, including a Turkish-made Zigana and a Pakistani Glock, along with 50 live rounds and a motorcycle from the encounter site.

Article Title: ‘What should I do with good weather?’: Woman prefers Hyderabad over Bengaluru traffic in viral video
Article Text:
Chetna questioned the appeal of Bengaluru’s pleasant weather when travelling within the city takes so long. (Photo credit: Instagram)





BENGALURU: A woman’s video criticising Bengaluru’s traffic has gone viral on Instagram, with her saying she has been “absolutely done” with the city’s congestion during her week-long stay.Chetna Singh, a digital creator who identifies herself as a software engineer at Microsoft in Hyderabad, shared a reel saying it takes her around 1.5-2 hours to travel from one place to another in Bengaluru.“Who says that Bangalore is better than Hyderabad?” she said in the video, adding that she is “absolutely freaking done” with the traffic.Singh questioned the appeal of Bengaluru’s pleasant weather when travelling within the city takes so long.“What should I do with the ‘good weather’ when I can’t go anywhere?” she said, before adding that she “just absolutely hate(s) the traffic here”.Singh said she had been in Bengaluru for the past one week and compared her experience with Hyderabad, saying, “Hyderabad is far better than Bangalore; I’m absolutely loving it.”Her Instagram caption also read: “Hyderabad is much better than Bangalore!!!”
Article Summary: Chetna Singh, a software engineer at Microsoft in Hyderabad, shared a reel saying it takes her around 1.5-2 hours to travel from one place to another in Bengaluru. “Who says that Bangalore is better than Hyderabad?” she said in the video.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board bans pigeon feeding, Tehri at shrines, tweaks order after uproar
Article Text:
In Kashmir bird feeding and distributing traditional Kashmiri yellow rice called Tehri is centuries old tradition.





SRINAGAR: As Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi today announced prohibition of the feeding of birds and distribution of food items within the premises of all Waqf shrines across Jammu and Kashmir, it has created uproar in the Valley with many describing the directive as unnecessary.Announcing the decision early Sunday Andrabi, who is senior BJP leader, said that devotees, visitors and others should strictly comply with the order. She said the restrictions were aimed at maintaining cleanliness, hygiene, sanctity and a peaceful environment at the shrines.According to her, feeding birds and distributing food items could attract stray animals, lead to unhygienic conditions and cause inconvenience or disturbance to devotees engaged in prayers and worship.J&K Waqf Board doesn’t come under the elected Jammu and Kashmir government. “I am asking people to not bring Tehri to any shrine and I am asking that there should be no bird feeding. And I am announcing a ban on both these things. People should cooperate,” she announced the directive while talking to the media.In Kashmir bird feeding and distributing traditional Kashmiri yellow rice called Tehri is centuries old tradition.Tehri is prepared with turmeric, salt and mustard oil or ghee and cooked in large quantities and then distributed to devotees, children and passersby at the shrines as an act of faith and charity and it holds immense cultural, emotional and spiritual significance. Political leaders are asking Andrabi to reconsider her decision.National Conference leader Salman Sagar described it as another bad and unfortunate decision of Waqf.” It is interference in a place with which people are emotionally and spiritually connected. They just want to destroy everything spiritual here. The Waqf Board should focus on infrastructure development, creating universities and hospitals providing clean washrooms and rest rooms around shrines, which she has not done.Only thing the BJP leader does is play politics as Waqf chairperson and play spiritual practices of people,” Sagar said. A PDP representative Arif Amin said Tehri and feeding pigeons are centuries-old Khanqah traditions. “Banning them in the name of cleanliness isn’t just about right or wrong, it’s about the hope and healing of people who have suffered,” he said. “You cannot clean a shrine by erasing its soul. Fiddling with faith is unacceptable,” he said.Many others, however, argued that pigeons are very aggressive and they multiply rapidly. “Wherever Pigeons flock and stay, other birds simply disappear. Eagles and kites used to keep pigeons in check but those birds have also completely disappeared. Pigeons are responsible for spreading many diseases including those related to the chest and lungs.”Others also reacted sharply forcing Andrabi to slightly change her verbal directions. “There is no blanket ban on pigeon feeding or Tehri distribution. There is no directive. It is my own request that it shouldn’t be done inside the shrine as it creates a huge problem for us with stray dogs entering into the shrines,” she said. “I myself believe in these traditions but there should be a proper way to feed birds and distribute rice and people should adhere to cleanliness norms,” Andrabi told the TOI.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi today announced prohibition of the feeding of birds and distribution of food items. In Kashmir bird feeding and distributing traditional Kashmiri yellow rice called Tehri is centuries old tradition. The ban has created uproar in the Valley with many describing the directive as unnecessary.

Article Title: Investment pitch or motor race? EPS says photos tell different story on CM Vijay’s UK visit
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay flags off Le Mans Cup at Silverstone during UK visit





TRICHY: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Sunday took a swipe at chief minister Vijay ’s UK visit, saying while the govt projected it as an effort to attract investments, photographs from there tell a different story.Speaking at an engagement ceremony of an AIADMK functionary in Trichy, EPS indirectly referred to photographs of Vijay flagging off a motor race at Silverstone.“It was believed that he was going to bring investments and improve the state’s economy. However, the photographs published in today’s newspapers tell a different story. Decide for yourself what they represent,” he said.He said no information or photo has come yet on the CM canvassing any business investment in London.Reiterating his allegations of horse-trading against the TVK govt, EPS likened AIADMK ‘turncoats’ to children lured with chocolates.“As a result, two constituencies have been notified for byelections. These are two constituencies won by AIADMK candidates with the effort of AIADMK cadres but because of horse-trading by TVK, they resigned, ” he said.EPS said the govt was surviving only because of MLAs from its alliance parties.“It would fall if their alliance parties withdraw. They are not standing on their own legs but with borrowed legs,” he said. Accusing the govt of failing to fulfil its poll promises, EPS said it was solely relying on social media reels instead.“It has been three years since the party was formed, but it has not done anything for the people. By doing nothing, TVK has come to power,” he said.
Article Summary: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami took a swipe at chief minister Vijay ’s UK visit. He said while the govt projected it as an effort to attract investments, photographs from there tell a different story. EPS indirectly referred to photographs of Vijay flagging off a motor race at Silverstone.

Article Title: ‘CM Vijay’ deepfake WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh
Article Text:
The manager offered Rs 11 lakh in aid, claiming that the money would be transferred to Giri’s account through Vijay’s foreign account in dollars. (AI Image)





BENGALURU: “I am CM Vijay. I am here to help you,” a voice and face appearing on a WhatsApp video call allegedly convinced a 29-year-old security guard that he was speaking to Tamil Nadu chief minister and actor C Joseph Vijay.Promised Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, the unsuspecting man ended up losing over Rs 1 lakh after a fraudster allegedly used a deepfake AI-generated video and repeatedly demanded processing fees and other payments. This is the first such case reported in the city.According to the complaint filed by Ratikanta Giri, a native of Odisha who has been working in the city for the last 20 years, he received a WhatsApp video call from the number 7986304658 on Sept 9. Soon after he answered the call, he saw Tamil Nadu CM “Vijay” introducing himself. The fraudster claimed he was providing financial aid to people facing economic hardship.“After introducing himself as CM Vijay in Hindi, I was asked about my name, profession and where I stay. After answering the questions, I was offered financial help from Vijay’s personal account,” he told TOI.“I refused any help, but the person on the video call repeatedly asked me to accept it, saying that he was helping many people.He then told me that his manager would contact me and that the funds would be transferred by him. He asked me to follow the instructions of his manager,” Giri said.The manager offered Rs 11 lakh in aid, claiming that the money would be transferred to Giri’s account through Vijay’s foreign account in dollars. Later, the ‘manager’ told him that Rs 5 lakh had been immediately allotted to him.Initially, Giri was asked to pay Rs 5,000 as exchange charges. Later, he was told that his PIN number had been locked and that he needed to pay Rs 18,000 to release it. When Giri refused, he was allegedly told that he would lose his earlier payment of Rs 5,000.Giri said, “I initially paid Rs 18,000. Later, another person claiming to be Thakur from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) contacted me and demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine imposed by the agency. Fearing I would lose my earlier payments, I transferred the money. I made a few more payments totalling over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app. When the fraudsters demanded another Rs 50,000, I refused and realised I had been duped. ”Giri later contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 before approaching Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act.To convince him to make the payments, the fraudsters sent Giri a letter claiming that Rs 5 lakh had been allotted to him. They also shared identity proof purportedly belonging to a CBI officer.“We urge people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims,” a senior officer said.
Article Summary: A fraudster allegedly used a deepfake AI-generated video and repeatedly demanded processing fees and other payments. Ratikanta Giri, a native of Odisha, received a WhatsApp video call from the number 7986304658 on Sept 9. The fraudster claimed he was providing financial aid to people facing economic hardship.

Article Title: Banned scavenging killed them; their families now wait years for Rs 30L relief
Article Text:
UP native Ratanlal Jaiswar’s son Chandan died in a septic tank in 2024. He has been living in Taloja, painting vehicles for a living and waiting for the compensation

Sewer deaths in Maharashtra





Arjun Chauhan (37) knows he should not be doing it. The contract worker from Panvel knows septic tanks and sewers are to be cleaned by machines, not people. He knows protective gear is mandatory. But when the call comes, he climbs in, with no safety cover.Chauhan has been doing this for 15-20 years, taking work from contractors, buildings and housing societies. A contractor pays him Rs 700-1,000 a day; others Rs 1,500-2,000. "There are lakhs like me who do this. After all, I have to put food on the table for my family," he said.His story is the reality behind the ban on manual scavenging: people continue to enter septic tanks, and when they die, their families spend years waiting for the statutory Rs 30 lakh compensation.For Ratanlal Jaiswar (54), that wait began in Dec 2024, when his son Chandan (22) died cleaning a septic tank at a chawl in Uran. Chandan, along with Vikas Kisan Tak (33) who too died, had entered the tank to rescue another worker who had collapsed inside.An FIR lodged was against the contractor, a suction-truck owner and one of the homeowners-all of whom had employed them to clean the tank without safety equipment.Nearly two years later, Ratanlal paints vehicles for a living and is awaiting the money.He wants to leave Taloja and return to UP, where his family is, and use the money to get his four children married. "I don't know how long I have to wait. Work dries up during monsoon, and when I don't find work, I sit here and sleep," he said.Tak's family is struggling too. They say the police initially refused to lodge an FIR, while the suction-truck owner offered to take care of the deceased's child's education. However, the family maintained that it wasn't enough as Tak was the sole breadwinner. His widow Archana (22), his mother and his sister Muskan now do domestic work to pay the rent for their room in Asudgaon, Panvel. Tak, who used to work as a driver-cleaner on the suction truck as well as do septic tank cleaning work, was paid Rs 17,000 a month, mostly in cash."I want my five-year-old son to complete his education. He is now my only hope to get out of this situation," Archana said.The same cycle has played out in other parts of Mumbai.In Powai, Akshay Mandal (23) andFulchand Kumar Saw (29) died in Nov 2025 while cleaning a sewage plant. "He was running the house. He used to send money so we could buy food and celebrate festivals," his father Jaynarayan, who travels to Mumbai from Jharkhand each year for work, says. Mandal's family got Rs 10 lakh from the contractor on humanitarian grounds but is awaiting the statutory compensation.Manual cleaning of manholes, septic tanks, and sewers is banned in India. But National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data shows 332 sanitation workers died in 18 states and UTs during hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks between Jan 1, 2021 and June 30, 2026. Maharashtra had the highest number of deaths at 58. Data tabled in the House in July 2025 by the state showed zero deaths in Mumbai between 2021 and 2024; a figure disputed by activists. Centre too has maintained that a survey found no manual scavengers in India."They want to hide the reality of caste-based discrimination. They don't accept the situation of Dalits who do scavenging," said Milind Ranade of Maharashtra Municipal Kamgar Union. He said the deaths reflect an indifference that has allowed the practice to persist. "The attitude remains: They are born to serve. Mar rahe hain, marne do."In the case of Jaiswar and Tak, the state said that since a private contractor engaged them, the compensation must be recovered from the employer. Bombay high court, however, held in Aug that the state must pay even when workers are privately engaged, and can recover it later from employers. It struck down Item 11 of 2019 and 2025 GRs, which forced private societies or contractors to pay instead of the state.Meanwhile, some families are awaiting enhanced compensation after Supreme Court, in 2023, raised it to Rs 30 lakh and directed govts to provide rehabilitation, including employment for next of kin and education for children.Nearly seven years after three workers died cleaning a tank in Govandi in 2019, each widow received Rs 10 lakh, but the balance has been pending. "It should've been released automatically. We have been trying to reach the authority, but there is no response. The approach remains casual," said advocate Abha Singh, who is pursuing the cases pro bono.Bezwada Wilson, national convenor of Safai Karmachari Andolan, says the delays show larger failure: "The govt has yet to acknowledge the extent to which manual scavenging continues, let alone identify those still trapped in it."But for those still doing the work, the distinction between what is legal and what happens on the ground is less important than the next day's wages. So when the next call comes, workers like Chauhan continue to climb into sewers.
Article Summary: Manual cleaning of manholes, septic tanks, and sewers is banned in India. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data shows 332 sanitation workers died in 18 states and UTs during hazardous cleaning. Maharashtra had the highest number of deaths at 58. Data tabled in the House in July 2025 by the state showed zero deaths in Mumbai.

Article Title: LeT founder Hafiz Saeed in Pakistan, aiding Kashmir terrorists: NIA; Jammu court issues non-bailable warrant
Article Text:
India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court

Hafiz Saeed terror case: How probe led to LeT founder

Jammu court issues second NBW against Hafiz Saeed

Hafiz Saeed's link to Pahalgam terror attack





JAMMU: Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder and India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is currently in Pakistan, the National Investigation Agency ( NIA ) told a Special Court in Jammu, which issued a second non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him in two months in connection with a terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror groups operating in Jammu and Kashmir.The NIA moved an application seeking an NBW against Saeed under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The LeT founder, a designated terrorist and resident of Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case.The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach on the outskirts of Srinagar earlier this year. A China-made grenade and 15 live rounds were recovered from Bhat, a resident of Batpora.Bhat was subsequently booked at Zakoora Police Station under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation into the case led to the busting of a terror network and the arrest of several more terrorists allegedly associated with LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF), along with two Pakistani nationals.According to the NIA, Saeed's alleged involvement emerged during the investigation.The agency said the arrested Pakistani terrorists were allegedly associated with him."Saeed is operating from Pakistan and providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists operating in the Kashmir Valley. The information is gathered that the said terrorist at present is in Pakistan and deliberately evading his arrest to escape the clutches of law," the NIA told the court.After hearing the NIA's submissions, Special Judge under the NIA Act Prem Sagar on September 8 observed that Saeed's involvement had emerged during the investigation and that he was "allegedly involved in terrorism."The court also noted that Saeed was at large and that the investigating agency had been unable to secure his attendance "in the ordinary manner". It subsequently issued a general non-bailable warrant against him.The latest warrant is the second NBW issued against Saeed by the Special NIA Court in Jammu in two months.Earlier, on July 8, the same court had issued an NBW against Saeed in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack in April, in which 25 tourists and a local resident were killed.Saeed is the founder of the proscribed LeT and a designated terrorist.The latest proceedings relate to the separate terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror operatives in the Union Territory.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court. The LeT founder, a designated terrorist, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case. The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach.

Article Title: Rape convict ex-MP Prajwal Revanna's smuggled jail phone contained multiple pornographic videos: Police
Article Text:
During the inspection, a prohibited mobile phone, SIM card, charger and notebook were found in a cell.





BENGALURU: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna , police sources told TOI on Saturday.Revanna, the former Hassan MP who is currently serving a sentence after being convicted in a sexual assault case, allegedly received a mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive in a coordinated smuggling operation involving five others, including a jail staffer, police said.All five people have been arrested in connection with the case, police said.Investigators said Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card.Jail warden Prakash Gawade allegedly handed the phone to Revanna personally. Undertrial prisoner Mohammed Tausif, who is accused in the DJ Halli case, allegedly concealed the SIM card in his mouth and passed it to Revanna, police said.Gawade allegedly handed over the charger and pen drive to Revanna during subsequent visits, investigators said. The jail staffer had previously been arrested and suspended on charges of allegedly smuggling ganja into the prison.In August, Central Crime Branch officers raided Revanna’s barrack and seized the mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive. An FIR was subsequently registered against Revanna and his co-inmate Pratap Rai.Rai, however, denied any involvement, saying Revanna had been using the mobile phone even before Rai joined him in the barrack.“While Naveen and Siddiqui arranged the phone and the Sim, Manjunath connected these men with Prajwal and Gawde. The four private persons and Prajwal said that besides paying money for mobile and Sim, they paid Rs 1 lakh (Rs 70,000 for mobile and Rs 30,000 for Sim) to Gawde,” an investigating officer told TOI.
Article Summary: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna. Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card. Five people have been arrested in connection with the case.

Article Title: 'Only tea was good': Near Jantar Mantar, Sonam Wangchuk appeals for support to Ladakh’s fight for democracy
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority for Ladakh’s future governance? Democratic representation Protection of land rights Safeguarding local culture Protecting the environment 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk early Saturday appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy, saying the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance at the September 9 meeting that major decisions concerning land allotment and local governance would not be taken by the current administration until a democratic government was formed in the Union Territory.The founder of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, supported Wangchuk, stating, “Stand with Ladakh!”“Hello friends, cockroaches, how are you? I am in Delhi and right next to the place where we spent weeks with you all, starving, yes, Jantar Mantar. But don’t worry. I am not here for any protest or fast. We came here from Ladakh for a meeting with the Home Ministry for a dialogue. The meeting has been going on for the preservation of the culture, nature and land of Ladakh, and this meeting was also part of it,” Wangchuk said in a message posted on social media early Saturday.Wangchuk shared a video of famous comedian Jaspal Bhatti, saying the meeting resulted in no new steps except fixing the date for the next meeting.“Only tea was good in the meeting, otherwise no new decision was made,” he said. He said decisions already taken, including the creation of a democratic structure in Ladakh under an assembly, were repeated. But he said the government did not provide any assurance that the process of the proposed Assembly would not be undermined by major decisions taken by the local administration and the office of the lieutenant governor in Ladakh.“We had only expected a small, legitimate assurance from the government that until a democratic structure is established in Ladakh, the UT administration should not take any major decisions that would change the face of Ladakh, whether it is land allotment or local governance. No major changes should be brought in these areas and it should be done in coordination with the democratic structure.”Wangchuk said if they get an assurance from the government within a week on the issue, they will celebrate the padyatra from September 19 to September 24 as “a memorial padyatra of the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for Ladakh.”“Otherwise, we will make it a big demonstration on behalf of the people of the entire country that justice should be done to Ladakh,” he said, adding that, as in every other state in the country, major decisions should be left to the people.On September 9, the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union government for administrative autonomy for Ladakh, held talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi.After the talks, chief secretary of Ladakh Ashish Kundra said the Centre had agreed to have a legislative body under Article 371 in the region, but it would require a constitutional amendment with a two-thirds majority in Parliament.“There was a discussion on whether there would be direct or indirect elections of the UT legislative body through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. Representatives of LAB and KDA said elections should be direct and a consensus was reached on this issue,” Kundra said at a press conference in Leh. “The question that remains to be answered concerns the relationship between the LAHDCs and the UT-level body. What powers will be vested in LAHDCs and what will be the jurisdiction of the UT-level body?”The chief secretary said the Centre had handed the Ladakh groups a list of eight to 10 questions to which they did not have immediate answers. “They were requested to think about those, consult the public and tell us what they think, so that we can move towards a draft by taking these issues forward at the next meeting in October,” he said.The chief secretary said the Centre did not want to impose any administrative model that was not acceptable to the people. “We want to move forward only after discussion with everyone. When in good faith and in the interest of everyone, everything is moving forward, it is the responsibility of the leadership here to create an environment of positivity among people, to give them hope that things are moving forward.”In a joint statement after the meeting, the LAB and KDA said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371. They said the MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.The groups, however, expressed concern about “developments taking place with respect to formation of new districts, creation of hill councils of each of the new districts, and other” major irreversible changes being made before an elected body at the Union Territory level.LAB and KDA said they unanimously opposed what they called “irreversible changes” being made to the administrative and political setup of Ladakh before the UT-level body was formed.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and the environment. The MHA set up the committee on January 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and more than 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in September last year.Wangchuk was accused of inciting the protesters. He was arrested, charged under the NSA and kept in Jodhpur jail. The Centre revoked his NSA detention in March this year. After his release, Wangchuk participated in the May 22 talks with the Centre. He was also one of the LAB representatives at the September 9 talks.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy. He said the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance at the September 9 meeting that major decisions concerning land allotment and local governance would not be taken.

Article Title: Shia cleric Yasoob Abbas meets Iranian President Pezeshkian, calls for stronger India-Iran ties
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maulana Yasoob Abbas, general secretary of the All India Shia Personal Law Board, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New Delhi and called for strengthening ties between India and Iran, his office said in a statement.Abbas welcomed Pezeshkian on behalf of the Shia community in India and handed him a letter seeking closer bilateral relations. He said India and Iran were ancient civilisations with longstanding cultural, intellectual, spiritual and trade links.According to the statement, Abbas sought greater cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy. He expressed hope that bilateral relations would strengthen further under Pezeshkian's leadership.The Shia cleric also raised concerns over tensions in West Asia and called for de-escalation and restoration of peace and stability in the region.Abbas expressed grief over the reported death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and condemned the killing of children, teachers and other civilians in an alleged attack on Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab.He also condemned terrorism, extremism and violence, saying the Indian Shia community stood for peace, dialogue, humanity and justice.Abbas expressed hope for peace, reconstruction and progress in Iran and said the historical relationship between India and Iran should be further expanded in the coming yearsSeparately, Maulana Kalbe Jawad Naqvi, general secretary of the Majlis-e-Ulama-e-Hind, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at a programme hosted in his honour at Delhi’s Oberoi hotel, according to a statement issued by Naqvi’s office. Naqvi congratulated Pezeshkian and paid tribute to the courage, resistance and sacrifices of the Iranian people in confronting oppressive forces.During his address, Naqvi spoke about Iran’s growing regional influence and called for further strengthening the friendly ties between India and Iran. He said closer cooperation between the two countries reflected the aspirations of their people. Several prominent personalities from different fields attended the programme.
Article Summary: Maulana Yasoob Abbas, general secretary of the All India Shia Personal Law Board, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Abbas sought greater cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy.

Article Title: Thousands in Texas were left without internet and TV after outage; Iranian hackers say we did it; AT&T says: No, we ...
Article Text:
AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

What AT&T says

Hackers warn of more attacks

AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

Thousands of users in Texas were left without internet, TV and phone services after an AT&T outage on Monday, September 7. An Iranian-linked hacking group later claimed responsibility for the disruption. The group, APT IRAN, said on Telegram that it had attacked telecommunications and other critical infrastructure in Texas. It also claimed responsibility for disrupting an unnamed water utility in the state. The claim was first reported by Threat Beat, a publication associated with the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University.According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN is closely linked to CyberAv3ngers, a group affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. The group said earlier attacks in late July targeted water systems in Minnesota, Michigan, Georgia, New Jersey, South Dakota and Arkansas. It then said those attacks were intended to warn about its ability to target critical US infrastructure.AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues. In an updated statement, the company rejected the hacking group's claim.“We have no evidence to support that claim. Our assessment indicates that attempted cable theft led to the outage. Internet service across Dallas and surrounding areas is operating normally, and we continue to monitor our network and review relevant information,” AT&T said.The company said internet service in Dallas and nearby areas had returned to normal.On August 30, the group claimed it would target more critical infrastructure. According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN said:"We had previously warned that anyone who encroaches on this soil and threatens our beloved Iran will pay for this mistake with their lives," The group also referred to earlier warnings involving Minnesota and said:"You ignored our warnings, and we in Minnesota warned you again. You ignored them again; but this time we will sew the lips and mouths of the American people together."The AT&T outage was first reported Monday, September 7 morning. According to Downdetector data cited by WFAA, customer reports began rising at about 2:18 a.m. A larger increase was recorded from around 10:30 a.m. Reports reached a peak of 5,990 shortly before 3 p.m. The number of reports then dropped quickly, with the outage mostly resolved by around 6 p.m.The outage affected internet, TV and phone services for some customers.
Article Summary: AT&T outage affects internet, TV and phone services for some customers. Iranian- linked hacking group claims responsibility for disruption. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.
